chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
The best abstemiousness is to conceal it.
ai.seo_question: What is the highest form of asceticism in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this maxim from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elevates *ikhfa'* (concealment) as the pinnacle of *zuhd*, distinguishing between mere asceticism and the refined spiritual state where one avoids the subtle vanity of being seen as ascetic. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *ikhlas* (sincerity), where the believer’s detachment from the world is so profound that even the act of detaching is hidden from public view to preserve the purity of intention before God.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 28. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
The best abstemiousness is to conceal it.
